title: Deuteronomy Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:1, what are the children of the LORD commanded not to do for the dead?
options: Not cut themselves or make any baldness between their eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Not cut themselves or make any baldness between their eyes
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:1 commands the children of the LORD not to cut themselves or make any baldness between their eyes for the dead.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 14:2 says that the LORD has chosen the people to be a peculiar people above all nations on earth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:2 states that the LORD hath chosen the people to be a peculiar people unto himself above all nations on earth.

questions.question: What type of things does Deuteronomy 14:3 forbid the people from eating?
questions.correctAnswer: Abominable things
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:3 commands that they shall not eat any abominable thing.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is listed in Deuteronomy 14:4 as one that may be eaten?
questions.correctAnswer: Ox
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:4 lists the ox, sheep, and goat among the beasts that may be eaten.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:5, which of these is NOT listed as an animal that may be eaten?
questions.correctAnswer: Camel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:5 lists hart, roebuck, fallow deer, wild goat, pygarg, wild ox, and chamois but does not include the camel.

questions.question: What two characteristics must a beast have to be eaten according to Deuteronomy 14:6?
options: Part the hoof and chew the cud
Have cloven hoof and not chew cud
questions.correctAnswer: Part the hoof and chew the cud
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:6 states that every beast that parteth the hoof, cleaveth the cleft into two claws, and cheweth the cud shall be eaten.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 14:7, the camel is clean because it chews the cud and divides the cloven hoof.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:7 explains the camel chews the cud but does not divide the hoof, so it is unclean.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 14:8 give for the swine being unclean?
options: It divideth the hoof but does not chew the cud
It chews the cud but does not divide the hoof
It has fins but no scales
questions.correctAnswer: It divideth the hoof but does not chew the cud
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:8 states the swine is unclean because it divideth the hoof but cheweth not the cud.

questions.question: Which aquatic creatures are allowed to be eaten according to Deuteronomy 14:9?
options: All that have fins and scales
All that swim in the water
questions.correctAnswer: All that have fins and scales
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:9 specifies that only those aquatic creatures with fins and scales are to be eaten.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 14:10 allows eating fish that do not have fins and scales.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:10 says whatsoever hath not fins and scales is unclean and may not be eaten.

questions.question: Which of these birds is specifically forbidden to be eaten according to Deuteronomy 14:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Eagle
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:12 lists the eagle among the birds that shall not be eaten.

questions.question: In Deuteronomy 14, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: You shall not cut yourselves nor make baldness for the dead
You shall tithe all the increase of your seed
You shall give the tithe to the Levite
questions.correctAnswer: You shall not cut yourselves nor make baldness for the dead
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:1 gives the command about not cutting or making baldness for the dead before any other instructions in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 14:6, beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud are clean to eat.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:6 clearly states that every beast that parteth the hoof and cheweth the cud shall be eaten.

questions.question: Which of these animals is allowed to be eaten according to the list in Deuteronomy 14:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Chamois
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:5 includes the chamois among the beasts that may be eaten.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:7, why are the camel, hare, and coney unclean?
options: They chew the cud but do not divide the hoof
They divide the hoof but do not chew the cud
They neither chew the cud nor divide the hoof
questions.correctAnswer: They chew the cud but do not divide the hoof
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:7 says these animals chew the cud but do not divide the hoof, making them unclean.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which birds are explicitly forbidden to be eaten according to Deuteronomy 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Eagle, ossifrage, ospray, and raven
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:12-14 lists the eagle, ossifrage, ospray, and raven among the birds that shall not be eaten. These verses clearly specify these birds as unclean.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14, what characteristic determines whether fish are clean to eat?
options: Must be caught with a net
questions.correctAnswer: Must have fins and scales
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:9-10 instructs that only fish with fins and scales are clean and may be eaten. Those without fins and scales are unclean.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 14:19 say about every creeping thing that flies?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:19 states that every creeping thing that flies is unclean and shall not be eaten, confirming the answer is True.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 14:20 guide the consumption of clean birds?
options: You may eat all clean fowls
Only birds caught by hand may be eaten
Birds must be offered as sacrifice before eating
Only young birds may be eaten
questions.correctAnswer: You may eat all clean fowls
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:20 states that all clean fowls may be eaten, indicating no further restriction beyond the clean/unclean classification.

questions.question: Which bird is specifically mentioned as unclean in Deuteronomy 14:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Bat
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:18 lists the bat among unclean creatures, distinguishing it from clean birds like dove or pigeon.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:21, what should be done with animals that die of themselves?
options: Give them to a stranger or sell to an alien
questions.correctAnswer: Give them to a stranger or sell to an alien
questions.explanation: The verse instructs not to eat animals that die of themselves but to give them to strangers or sell to aliens, emphasizing holiness and obedience.

questions.question: What virtue is taught by the instruction in Deuteronomy 14:23 to eat the tithe before the LORD in the place He chooses?
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience and reverence toward God
questions.explanation: Eating the tithe before the LORD in the chosen place teaches obedience and reverence, as stated in Deuteronomy 14:23 emphasizing learning to fear God always.

questions.question: If the place chosen by the LORD to eat the tithe is too far to carry it, what does Deuteronomy 14:24-25 instruct to do?
options: Turn the tithe into money and go to the place to spend it
Leave the tithe at home and fast instead
Send someone else to carry the tithe
questions.correctAnswer: Turn the tithe into money and go to the place to spend it
questions.explanation: These verses explain that if the place is too far, the tithe should be converted to money and taken to the LORD’s chosen place to be spent there joyfully.

questions.question: What is the purpose of eating the tithe before the LORD as described in Deuteronomy 14:23 and 26?
options: To rejoice and learn to fear the LORD always
questions.correctAnswer: To rejoice and learn to fear the LORD always
questions.explanation: The passages instruct rejoicing before the LORD and learning to fear Him always through the practice of bringing and eating tithes.

questions.question: Who, besides the family, is specifically mentioned in Deuteronomy 14:27-29 as beneficiaries of the tithe?
options: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Verses 27-29 identify these four groups as recipients of the tithe, reflecting God's concern for those with no inheritance or provision.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 14:7, animals that chew the cud but do not have cloven hooves, such as the camel, are considered clean.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:7 specifies that animals like the camel chew the cud but do not have cloven hooves and are therefore unclean.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 14 teach the virtue of generosity and care for others through the instructions about tithe?
options: By instructing the sharing of tithes with Levites, strangers, orphans, and widows
By demanding all tithe be given only to priests
By encouraging accumulation of tithe for personal wealth
By allowing tithe to be kept secret
questions.correctAnswer: By instructing the sharing of tithes with Levites, strangers, orphans, and widows
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:27-29 shows generosity by ensuring the tithe supports those without inheritance, teaching care and compassion.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:8, why is the swine considered unclean?
options: Because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud
Because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof
questions.correctAnswer: Because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud
questions.explanation: Verse 8 clearly states the swine has divided hoof but does not chew the cud, making it unclean according to the law.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 14:1 prohibit in relation to mourning customs?
options: Cutting oneself or making baldness between the eyes for the dead
Wearing black clothes for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting oneself or making baldness between the eyes for the dead
questions.explanation: Verse 1 forbids cutting or shaving the head in mourning, emphasizing Israel’s identity as God's holy children.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 14:2 describes Israel as a peculiar people chosen above all nations.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 2 affirms that Israel is a holy and peculiar people chosen by the LORD above all nations, highlighting their special status.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:21, what is forbidden concerning the flesh of animals that die of themselves?
questions.correctAnswer: You shall not eat it
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:21 commands not to eat anything that dies of itself; instead, it should be given to the stranger or sold to an alien.

questions.question: What is the purpose of eating the tithe before the LORD at the place He will choose, as stated in Deuteronomy 14:23?
options: To learn to fear the LORD thy God always
questions.correctAnswer: To learn to fear the LORD thy God always
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:23 explains that eating the tithe at the LORD's chosen place is so that one may learn to fear God always.

questions.question: If the place chosen by the LORD is too far to carry the tithe, what does Deuteronomy 14:25 instruct the people to do?
options: Turn it into money and carry the money to the place
Give the tithe to the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Turn it into money and carry the money to the place
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:25 instructs that if the place is too far, the tithe should be converted into money which is then carried to the place the LORD chooses.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:27, why must the Levite not be forsaken?
options: Because he has no part nor inheritance with you
Because he is the king's messenger
questions.correctAnswer: Because he has no part nor inheritance with you
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:27 states the Levite must not be forsaken because he has no inheritance or share in the land.

questions.question: What is one of the uses for the money obtained by converting the tithe, according to Deuteronomy 14:26?
options: To pay taxes to the king
questions.correctAnswer: To buy oxen or sheep
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:26 allows the money from the tithe to be spent on oxen, sheep, wine, or anything the soul desires.

questions.question: Which groups of people are specifically mentioned in Deuteronomy 14:29 as coming to eat and be satisfied from the tithe laid up within the gates?
options: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
The priests, the elders, and the king
questions.correctAnswer: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:29 specifically names these groups as beneficiaries of the tithe stored within the gates.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk' in Deuteronomy 14:21 symbolize in later biblical law and Christian theology?
options: A prohibition against mixing life and death, later applied to kosher dietary laws
A command to always cook meat thoroughly
An instruction to avoid eating dairy products
questions.correctAnswer: A prohibition against mixing life and death, later applied to kosher dietary laws
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:21's phrase is understood as forbidding mixing meat and dairy, foundational to kosher laws and discussed in later texts like Exodus 23:19 and in Christian dietary discussions.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage closely connects with the tithe instructions found in Deuteronomy 14:22-29?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 27:30-33
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:30-33 also discusses tithes and offerings, paralleling the instructions in Deuteronomy 14 about tithing and support for the Levites.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 14:21-29 uses an inclusio literary device framing the chapter’s laws about clean and unclean foods and tithes. What is an inclusio?
options: A literary device where a passage is bracketed by similar phrases or themes
A type of prophecy about future events
A metaphor comparing two unlike things
questions.correctAnswer: A literary device where a passage is bracketed by similar phrases or themes
questions.explanation: The passage frames the laws on food and tithes with similar themes at beginning and end, an inclusio creating emphasis and structure (Deuteronomy 14:1 and Deuteronomy 14:29).

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'peculiar people' in Deuteronomy 14:2 denotes a people chosen and set apart?
questions.correctAnswer: 'Segullah'
questions.explanation: The Hebrew 'Segullah' in Deuteronomy 14:2 means treasured possession or peculiar people, denoting God's chosen status of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 14:28 commands that the tithe of the increase must be brought every year and laid up within the gates.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:28 specifies the tithe is brought at the end of three years, not annually.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 14:9-10, all creatures in the waters without fins and scales are considered unclean and may not be eaten.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:9-10 clearly states that only creatures with fins and scales are clean and allowed to be eaten.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the teaching of not eating things that have died by themselves as found in Deuteronomy 14:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 15:20
questions.explanation: Acts 15:20 reiterates the prohibition concerning eating blood and things strangled or dead, reflecting Deuteronomy 14:21's dietary laws.

questions.question: What historical-cultural significance does the instruction in Deuteronomy 14:21 about not seething a kid in its mother's milk have in the Ancient Near East context?
options: It distinguished Israelite dietary laws from Canaanite pagan practices
It was a common practice in Israelite feasts
It prohibited the use of dairy in any meal
questions.correctAnswer: It distinguished Israelite dietary laws from Canaanite pagan practices
questions.explanation: The prohibition in Deuteronomy 14:21 served to set Israel apart from neighboring peoples who practiced mixing meat and milk in rituals, marking cultural and religious distinctiveness.

questions.question: How does the theme of holiness in Deuteronomy 14:1-2 develop earlier Scripture teachings about Israel's identity?
options: It builds on Exodus 19:6 where Israel is called a holy nation chosen by God
It contradicts the idea that Israel is chosen
It introduces a new concept not found earlier
It focuses only on dietary laws
questions.correctAnswer: It builds on Exodus 19:6 where Israel is called a holy nation chosen by God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:1-2 reiterates and develops Exodus 19:6’s teaching about Israel as a holy and chosen people set apart for God.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is demonstrated by God's choice of Israel as described in Deuteronomy 14:2?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and sovereignty
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:2 declares that Israel is a holy people chosen by the LORD above all nations, demonstrating God's sovereign selection for holiness and covenant relationship.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:6, what combination of characteristics must a land animal have to be considered clean and edible?
options: Divides the hoof and chews the cud
Is a creeping thing that flies
questions.correctAnswer: Divides the hoof and chews the cud
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:6 states that animals which part the hoof and chew the cud are clean and allowed to be eaten, highlighting God’s criteria for clean land animals.

questions.question: What theological principle can be drawn from the prohibition in Deuteronomy 14:21 against eating anything that dies of itself and the instruction to give it to a stranger or sell it?
options: Respect for life and communal provision
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for life and communal provision
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:21 teaches respect for life by prohibiting consumption of carrion and promotes social justice by instructing the provision for strangers and aliens, integrating holiness with community care.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 14:22-23 connect the doctrine of tithing with the believer's relationship to God?
options: Tithing is a legalistic burden with no spiritual benefit
Tithing fosters dependence on human effort
Tithing is an act of worship to cultivate reverence for God
Tithing is only for priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Tithing is an act of worship to cultivate reverence for God
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 link tithing the produce to eating before the LORD in His chosen place, teaching that tithes cultivate fear (reverence) of God and acknowledge His provision and presence.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's provision and holiness do Deuteronomy 14:9 and 14:10 convey regarding aquatic creatures?
options: Only creatures with fins and scales are clean and reflect God's order
All sea creatures are clean and permissible
Only shellfish are acceptable for consumption
Aquatic creatures are not addressed in God's law
questions.correctAnswer: Only creatures with fins and scales are clean and reflect God's order
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:9-10 specify that only aquatic animals with fins and scales are clean, reflecting God's design and order in creation and setting boundaries for holiness in diet.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 14:7-8, why are animals such as the camel, hare, and swine considered unclean?
options: They chew the cud but do not have divided hooves, or vice versa
They are too small to be clean
questions.correctAnswer: They chew the cud but do not have divided hooves, or vice versa
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 explain that clean animals must both chew the cud and have divided hooves; camels and hares chew cud but lack divided hooves, swine have divided hooves but do not chew cud, thus are unclean.

questions.question: What does the prohibition against cutting oneself or making baldness between the eyes in Deuteronomy 14:1 symbolize in terms of sanctification?
options: Rejecting pagan mourning practices and maintaining holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Rejecting pagan mourning practices and maintaining holiness
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 14:1 forbids mourning practices like cutting or baldness that were associated with pagan rituals, emphasizing Israel's calling to holiness and separation from idolatrous customs.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by Deuteronomy 14:27-29 regarding the support of Levites and marginalized groups?
options: Doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
Doctrine of social justice and provision for the vulnerable
Doctrine of strict separation from strangers
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of social justice and provision for the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Verses 27-29 teach that Levites, strangers, orphans, and widows must be provided for through tithes, showing God's concern for social justice and care for the vulnerable within the covenant community.

questions.question: How does the instruction in Deuteronomy 14:25-26 about converting tithes into money and rejoicing before the LORD reveal God's gracious provision?
options: God restricts worship to a single way
God permits flexibility in worship to meet human needs and encourages joy
God forbids spending tithes on anything but animals
God requires tithes to be stored indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: God permits flexibility in worship to meet human needs and encourages joy
questions.explanation: These verses allow the tithe to be converted into money if the place of worship is distant, showing God's gracious accommodation and the importance of rejoicing in His presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about holiness and community care is taught by Deuteronomy 14:20 and Deuteronomy 14:19 on clean birds and flying creeping things?
options: All flying creatures are clean and to be eaten
Clean birds are permitted, but flying creeping things are unclean, emphasizing separation and holiness
Flying creeping things must be eaten to maintain purity
There is no distinction between birds and flying creeping things
questions.correctAnswer: Clean birds are permitted, but flying creeping things are unclean, emphasizing separation and holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 20 permits eating clean birds, while verse 19 forbids flying creeping things, demonstrating God's call to holiness through dietary distinctions and communal purity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the dietary laws in Deuteronomy 14 are arbitrary and irrelevant to spiritual life. What does Deuteronomy 14:3-8 actually teach about God's purpose in these laws?
options: They are arbitrary rules without meaning
They are designed to separate Israel as a holy people and teach discipline
They focus only on health benefits
They are outdated and not meant for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They are designed to separate Israel as a holy people and teach discipline
questions.explanation: Verses 3-8 prohibit eating abominable things and define clean animals, demonstrating God's intent to set Israel apart as holy through obedience, not arbitrary regulation (cf. Leviticus 11 for further context).

questions.question: What does the instruction in Deuteronomy 14:21 about not seething a kid in its mother's milk signify in terms of ethical sanctification?
options: A ritual of pagan fertility worship
A prohibition against mixing life and death in an unnatural way
An economic law about milk sales
A dietary suggestion without moral weight
questions.correctAnswer: A prohibition against mixing life and death in an unnatural way
questions.explanation: The prohibition in verse 21 symbolically forbids blending life (milk) and death (the kid being cooked), reflecting God's call to ethical sanctification and respect for creation’s order.

questions.question: What does the inclusion of the stranger, fatherless, and widow in Deuteronomy 14:29 teach about God's covenant community?
options: God's covenant is exclusive to Israel only
God's covenant includes care and provision for marginalized and vulnerable within the community
They are to be excluded from covenant blessings
They must support themselves without help
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant includes care and provision for marginalized and vulnerable within the community
questions.explanation: Verse 29 emphasizes that the vulnerable such as strangers, orphans, and widows are included in God's provision through tithes, illustrating the covenant's social justice dimension.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 14:4-5 contribute to the biblical theology of God's creation and providence?
options: It lists random animals without theological meaning
It reflects God's orderly provision of specific animals for food, demonstrating His care
It forbids all animals from being eaten
It focuses solely on ritual sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's orderly provision of specific animals for food, demonstrating His care
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 list specific clean animals God provides for food, revealing His providence and order in creation to sustain His covenant people.

questions.question: What synthesis can be made between Deuteronomy 14:22 and 14:28 regarding the handling of tithes and their purpose in the community?
options: Tithes are only for personal wealth
Tithes are collected yearly and stored for communal support every three years
Tithes are used for temple construction only
questions.correctAnswer: Tithes are collected yearly and stored for communal support every three years
questions.explanation: Verse 22 commands yearly tithing of increase, and verse 28 instructs that at the end of three years tithes are to be brought and stored within the gates for Levites and needy, showing a system of provision and community care.
